Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of painful, itchy, cracked skin of the palms, worsening recently and interfering with work; suspected contact/irritant dermatitis related to cleaning products. Topical steroid and emollients prescribed; avoidance measures advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful, itchy, dry, cracked skin on palms for ~3–4 months; worsened recently.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent itching; bleeding only after scratching. Mild generalized dryness on legs (longstanding).
- Pertinent negatives: No fever, nausea/vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms. Appetite and general wellbeing maintained.
- Impact: Unable to work for the past 3 days.
- Triggers/exposures: Works as a hotel housekeeper; frequent exposure to cleaning products; often not wearing gloves; job change ~4 months ago.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug or other allergies reported.
- Family history: Diabetes; no known skin disease; no asthma or bowel disease.
- Social history: Non-smoker; drinks a couple of pints of alcohol per week. Occupational exposure as above.
- Prior treatments: E45 emollient (ineffective). OTC antihistamine (ineffective).

Examination:

Impression:
- Suspected contact/irritant dermatitis of the hands (palms), likely occupational exposure to cleaning products; background xerosis. Type 2 diabetes as comorbidity.

Plan:
- Avoidance: Wear protective gloves at all times when cleaning; minimize exposure to cleaning agents.
- Medications:
  - Topical steroid cream prescribed (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Stronger emollient prescribed; apply generously 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
- Follow-up: Reassess in 10–14 days if not improved; return sooner if worsening, spreading, or increased dryness.
- Prescription: Sent to patient’s pharmacy.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals and skin examination not documented; specific steroid and emollient names and dosing (for steroid) not documented; comprehensive medication reconciliation (only metformin listed) not completed; diabetes control parameters not discussed; vaccination status not addressed.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some unclear/inaudible segments and interruptions; overall sufficient to determine history and plan.
